Can the models recover severe mortality at high DHW?

Event-held-out comparison of the formal benchmark and shape-aware candidates

The candidate being tested

The shape-aware candidate is not a forced 50% mortality rule. It makes four specific changes and leaves the existing benchmark untouched:

  • proportional Acropora cover is the primary community-susceptibility term;
  • total preceding coral cover replaces the strongly correlated absolute Acropora-cover term;
  • the response can steepen above 8 DHW and the DHW–Acropora interaction enters both mortality occurrence and positive magnitude;
  • event identity is excluded from the ecological mean so it cannot absorb a relationship that must transfer to a future event.

The BRT additionally constrains DHW and proportional Acropora effects to be non-decreasing, gives each reef-year equal fitting weight, and tunes against overall, event-balanced, and high-DHW errors. The Bayesian model uses directional but non-binding ecological priors.

Recommended production route

No single candidate wins for every observation programme. The recommended predictor therefore uses the best event-held-out route for each programme and does not ask a tree model to extrapolate beyond the largest DHW in its training data.

Programme-specific model routing rule
Programme Within observed DHW support Beyond observed DHW support Reason
LTMP benthic Shape-aware ensemble Shape-aware BRMS Shape ensemble improves overall and severe-tail validation; use BRMS alone beyond tree training support.
Manta tow Benchmark ensemble Benchmark BRMS Shape candidate worsens event-held-out calibration; retain the benchmark and drop its BRT outside support.
MMP inshore Shape-aware BRMS Shape-aware BRMS Shape BRMS has the best overall, severe-tail, and 2024 event-held-out performance.

This promotes the shape-aware ensemble for LTMP within support, retains the benchmark for manta tow, and promotes the shape-aware BRMS for MMP. BRMS alone is used beyond observed DHW support because boosted trees cannot extrapolate a new dose-response slope.

Does 12 DHW now produce ecologically plausible mortality?

The production curves below use all five events for fitting. “Acropora dominated” means 90% proportional Acropora and 55% total pre-event coral cover; other attainable predictors are held at programme-specific medians. These are scenario predictions, not a replacement for held-out validation.

Promotion requires more than producing a steeper curve. The candidate must improve held-out high-DHW and severe-loss calibration, retain acceptable overall error, avoid inflating the low-mortality 2020/22 events, and pass all sampling diagnostics. Any failure remains visible rather than being averaged away by the production scenario.
